description: OpenAPI Overlays across the catalog. Documents applied on top of an API contract to add or change what it says. meta says who wrote it (authorship: provider / derived / generated / unmarked), whether the provider hosts it (provider_hosted — the only kind the Kin Score credits), what the actions touch (purpose), the action counts and the contract it extends. Filter by q / tags / providers; include=["content"] inlines bodies. Use find_artifacts for cross-type search.

authorship.description: Who wrote the overlay: "provider" (published or hosted by the provider), "derived" (API Evangelist, from the provider's contracts), "generated" (API Evangelist tooling — most are conversational phrasing), "unmarked" (no record; never presented as the provider's).

context.description: Optional: why you are asking. One sentence — the task you are trying to complete, or what you expect to get back. Never included in the answer and never used to rank; it is read only when a result turns out to be wrong, which is when knowing the intent is what makes the report actionable.

purpose.description: What the actions touch: "phrasing" (x-apievangelist-phrasing per operation), "servers", "documentation", "security", "removal", "update".

sort.description: Order: relevance / provider / name, or action_count / target_count (largest first).

tags.description: Tag slugs. On PROVIDERS this is identity — what the company says it does, from its own apis.yml. A resource or operation term (webhook, saml, order, oai-pmh) will correctly match no provider; use find_apis?tags= for those, or find_providers?api_tags= to reach companies whose APIs merely touch it.

name: find_overlays
